Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for a 45-year-old woman with 2 weeks of right knee pain and clicking associated with increased running; advised rest/ice, prescribed a stronger anti-inflammatory (details not documented), and referred to physiotherapy with return precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain and clicking during exercise; intermittent tingling in right toes after a run (single episode).
- Onset/duration: ~2 weeks.
- Course: Worsening with recent runs; last run required stopping due to pain. No current pain at rest; clicking not present at rest today but noted during gym activities (with knee flexion/extension during ab exercises).
- Activity context: Began marathon training ~1 month ago; runs 4–5 miles with a few 7–8 mile runs. Also goes to gym several times/week. Plays sports, including ice hockey.
- Location/character: Pain felt centrally, sometimes perceived toward the right side of the right knee.
- Swelling: Mild swelling after first run resolved with ice; no current swelling.
- Mechanical symptoms: Clicking with flexion/extension during gym work. No locking. No true giving way/instability reported.
- Function: Pain begins ~20 minutes into running (~2.5–3 miles). No difficulty with stairs or walking. Full ability to fully flex and extend per patient report.
- Neurologic/vascular: Single episode of tingling in right toes after a run; resolved. No color or temperature changes in lower legs. No calf pain.
- Edema: Notices sock indentations after prolonged standing; pitting not assessed.
- Associated symptoms: Denies back pain and other joint pains or swelling.
- Prior injury: Fall while playing ice hockey a few months ago resulting in a large bruise; no ongoing issues reported.
- ROS pertinent negatives: No fever, systemic illness, GI issues, asthma, indigestion, or acid reflux.

Past Medical History:
- Hyperopia; status post LASIK surgery.
- History of severe UTI; evaluated in ER (suspected kidney stones at the time). No ongoing issues reported.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed (dose noted; route/frequency not documented).
- Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Aleve (naproxen; dose/route/frequency not documented; patient uncertain about drug class).
- Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- New prescription: “Stronger anti-inflammatory” to be taken regularly instead of ibuprofen; take with food (drug name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Very physically active; training for a marathon; goes to the gym several times/week; plays ice hockey.
- Tobacco: Not documented.
- Alcohol: Not documented.
- Recreational drugs: Occasionally “smokes a joint” (cannabis).
- Residence: London address provided.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded.
- No physical exam findings documented (video consult without formal exam).

Investigations:
- None performed or reviewed during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Right knee pain with exertion and clicking in the context of increased running (possible overuse injury; exact diagnosis not established via video).
  - Plan:
    - Continue ice therapy regularly.
    - Modify training: ease up on running; avoid running through pain; stop activity if pain necessitates stopping.
    - Start prescribed stronger anti-inflammatory regularly instead of ibuprofen; take with food; do not combine with ibuprofen.
    - Referral to physiotherapy for comprehensive assessment and examination.
    - Consider imaging (to assess cartilage/other structures) based on in-person assessment/physio findings.
    - If physiotherapy wait is long, arrange clinic visit for in-person evaluation.
    - Urgent care/return precautions: persistent swelling, heat, redness of the knee, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.
- Issue 2: Transient tingling in right toes post-run (resolved).
  - Plan:
    - Monitor; no specific treatment initiated during this visit.

General Plan items:
- Prescription for a stronger anti-inflammatory sent to pharmacy (details not documented).
- Physiotherapy referral placed.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Medication reconciliation (full doses/routes/frequencies), allergies, surgical history beyond LASIK, vitals, detailed musculoskeletal exam, smoking and alcohol history, occupation, family history.
- Internal conflicts: Patient uncertainty regarding Aleve’s drug class noted; no other conflicts identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear; no significant audio issues reported.
